## Mathematical basis of stability analysis

$$\begin{aligned}
\dot{x} &= f(x, y) \\
\dot{y} &= g(x, y)
\end{aligned} \qquad \text{system of two coupled differential equations}$$

step 1 $\quad \downarrow \quad$ find nullclines and fixed point(s)

$$\begin{aligned}
\dot{x} = 0 &\rightarrow f(x_o, y_o) = 0 \\
\dot{y} = 0 &\rightarrow g(x_o, y_o) = 0
\end{aligned}$$

step 2 $\quad \downarrow \quad$ consider small deviation from fixed point

$$\begin{aligned}
\tilde{x} &\equiv x - x_o \\
\tilde{y} &\equiv y - y_o
\end{aligned}$$

---

$$\begin{aligned}
\tilde{x} &\equiv x - x_o \\
\tilde{y} &\equiv y - y_o
\end{aligned} \qquad \text{consider small deviation from fixed point}$$

step 3 $\quad \downarrow \quad$ linearize around fixed point(s)

$$\begin{aligned}
\dot{x} &\approx \tilde{x} \left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right|_{(x_o, y_o)} + \tilde{y} \left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}\right|_{(x_o, y_o)} \equiv a\tilde{x} + b\tilde{y} \\
\dot{y} &\approx \tilde{x} \left.\frac{\partial g}{\partial x}\right|_{(x_o, y_o)} + \tilde{y} \left.\frac{\partial g}{\partial y}\right|_{(x_o, y_o)} \equiv c\tilde{x} + d\tilde{y}
\end{aligned}$$

step 4 $\quad \downarrow \quad$ determine matrix A

$$A = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$$

---

$$A = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix} \qquad \text{determine matrix A}$$

step 5 $\quad \downarrow \quad$ determine trace and determinant of A:

$$\begin{aligned}
\tau &= \text{trace}(A) = a + d \\
\Delta &= \det(A) = ad - bc
\end{aligned}$$

step 6 $\quad \downarrow \quad$ determine stability of fixed point

only if $\tau < 0$ and $\Delta > 0$, $(x_o, y_o)$ is a stable fixed point

!!! be careful: only valid for 2 dimensional systems !!!

## I Phosphorylation (CheA, CheY, CheB)

**CheA** (protein kinase), uses ATP to  
phosphorylate one of its histidines.

$$\text{CheA} + \text{ATP} \leftrightarrow \text{CheA}_{\text{p}} + \text{ADP}$$

**CheA ($\text{CheA}_{\text{p}}$)is bound to the Tar receptor  
through an adapter protein CheW. CheW is  
not known to have any enzymatic activity.  
(these proteins are sometimes called  
'scaffolding protein')**

**$\text{CheA}_{\text{p}}$ is unstable and transfers its  
phosphoryl group to CheY (highly soluble,  
diffuses through the cytoplasm**

## I Phosphorylation (CheA, CheY, CheB)

autophosphorylation: $\quad \text{CheA} + \text{ATP} \leftrightarrow \text{CheA}_{\text{p}} + \text{ADP}$

phosphoryltransfer: $\quad \text{CheA}_{\text{p}} + \text{CheY} \leftrightarrow \text{CheA} + \text{CheY}_{\text{p}}$

CheYp binds to the motor (FliM),  
motor rotates CW (= tumbles)

*logic:*

high levels of CheA -> high levels of CheYp  
(lots of tumbles)

low levels of CheA -> low levels of CheYp  
(straight swimming)
